title: Advertisements, quotations, catalogs, and offers
summary: Specific limitations can make an advertisement an offer, while many advertisements invite further orders.
notes: Lefkowitz specifies an item, a price, and a first-come mechanism that leaves nothing open. The Moulton note asks how an unbounded quantity affects a quotation’s apparent commitment. The coin-allocation problem tests whether receipt or confirmation of an order is acceptance. Geismar illustrates that a consumer statute may supply relief even if ordinary offer-and-acceptance analysis supplies no contract.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 198–205. Open assigned page 198.
